note: Entries are drafts for Pipeline C: hours, cost and ticketUrl are null, never placeholders. Coordinates carry their resolve-pin confidence; LOW or none entries must be re-pinned before applying. No Tasmanian ids exist in the app or in git history for these slugs.

proposed_destinations.name: West Coast Tasmania
proposed_destinations.coordinates_source: centre of its spots (Strahan, Queenstown, Zeehan); not a gazetteer point
proposed_destinations.name_evidence: Discover Tasmania has a 'West Coast' regional page (https://www.discovertasmania.com.au/regions/west-coast, a counted source for Strahan); Wikivoyage 'Strahan' calls it 'the regional hub of the West Coast' and Wikivoyage 'Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park' says 'in the West Coast of Tasmania'; Wikipedia 'West Coast, Tasmania'. Wikivoyage has no West Coast page of its own (only 'Western Tasmania'), so the name rests on the tourism-board region; owner to confirm the display name (e.g. 'West Coast Tasmania' to avoid NZ West Coast).
proposed_destinations.shape_note: Named region rather than Strahan alone: Strahan's draws (Sarah Island, Gordon River, Ocean Beach, Hogarth Falls) are neighbours, and Queenstown, Zeehan and Montezuma Falls are 25-40 km away. Strahan and Queenstown are spots because each town has its own draws. All spots within 75% (52 km) of the centre; Sarah Island is furthest at about 40 km.
proposed_destinations.needs: description, 2-3 reasons with photos, tips, best months, header (Pipeline C); a proposal only, not added.

proposed_destinations.name: Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park
proposed_destinations.coordinates_source: visual centre of the Lyell Highway section where visitors reach the park (Nelson Falls to Frenchmans Cap trailhead)
proposed_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage page 'Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park' ('The main draw of the park is Nelson Falls'); Parks Tasmania national park; Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area.
proposed_destinations.shape_note: Every national park is a destination; exactly four kept spots clear the bar. Gordon River is inside the park but is reached by Strahan cruise, so it is a West Coast spot. Overlaps the West Coast destination's span near Queenstown: park visitors come along the Lyell Highway, West Coast visitors base at Strahan/Queenstown.
proposed_destinations.needs: description, reasons with photos, tips, best months, header (Pipeline C); proposal only.

proposed_destinations.name: Southwest National Park
proposed_destinations.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article centre (park centroid, rounded); main visitor hub is Strathgordon/Scotts Peak
proposed_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage page 'Southwest National Park' ('accounting for 10% of Tasmania'); Wikipedia; Parks Tasmania.
proposed_destinations.shape_note: ONLY THREE kept spots (Melaleuca and Port Davey are review). Proposed under the flagship exemption (World Heritage wilderness covering a tenth of the state, like Fiordland); if the owner does not accept the exemption, these three are standalone and the park itself a standalone spot. Cockle Creek is owned by tas-hobart-southeast; Recherche Bay is rejected.

placements.name: Sarah Island
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon place=islet 'Sarah Island' within 100 m of Wikipedia (Macquarie Harbour Penal Station)
placements.reason: Macquarie Harbour island reached by cruise from Strahan; inside the West Coast span and reached from that base.
placements.bio: The ruins of an 1822 convict penal station on a Macquarie Harbour island, visited on a cruise from Strahan.

placements.name: Gordon River
placements.coordinates_source: none: resolve-pin found no feature. Pin should be the cruise landing (Heritage Landing) from the operator or Parks Tasmania; Wikipedia gives no usable point
placements.reason: Reached only by river cruise from Strahan (Wikivoyage Strahan), so it is a spot of the West Coast base, not of Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park, which it lies in.
placements.bio: A rainforest river in Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park, visited by cruise from Strahan.

placements.name: Strahan
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin LOW; point is Strahan Historic Foreshore Walking Track (photon highway=footway) on the waterfront; Wikipedia town point (-42.15,145.3167) is the town centre. Pipeline C to confirm a waterfront point
placements.reason: The town itself is a draw (waterfront, foreshore walk, Regatta Point); kept as a spot because the destination is the West Coast region, not the town. Its cruises and railway are not listed beside it as vehicles.
placements.bio: A Macquarie Harbour fishing port with a historic waterfront and foreshore walk, the base for Gordon River cruises.

placements.name: Queenstown
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon place=town 'Queenstown' agrees with Wikipedia; town centre point, acceptable for a town spot
placements.reason: The town has several open attractions of its own and a historic main street; reached on the Lyell Highway within the West Coast span (about 16 km from Iron Blow Lookout).
placements.bio: A former copper-mining town ringed by bare mined hills, with a historic main street and mine tours.

placements.name: Ocean Beach
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin LOW: photon leisure=nature_reserve 'Ocean Beach Conservation Area'; no natural=beach feature returned. Needs OSM beach or the access car park confirmed
placements.reason: A 40 km surf beach reached by road from Strahan, inside the West Coast span.
placements.bio: A 40 km surf beach of huge dunes and Southern Ocean swell north-west of Strahan, with dangerous swimming.

placements.name: Montezuma Falls
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon waterway=waterfall 'Montezuma Falls' near Wikipedia point
placements.reason: Reached from Zeehan/Rosebery on the old tramway walk, inside the West Coast span.
placements.bio: Tasmania's highest waterfall at over 104 m, reached by an 11.5 km return walk along an old tramway.

placements.name: Iron Blow Lookout
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=viewpoint 'Iron Blow Lookout' within 100 m of Wikipedia
placements.reason: A short roadside viewpoint above Queenstown, reached from there.
placements.bio: A lookout over the Iron Blow, the huge mine pit above Queenstown where the area's mining began.

placements.name: Zeehan
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin LOW: photon place=town 'Zeehan' (town centre)
placements.reason: A one-street silver-mining town with a surviving heritage streetscape; kept beside its museum because the streetscape is a draw the museum does not cover (as Eden's waterfront). Within the West Coast span (about 25 km from Strahan).
placements.bio: A former silver-mining boomtown whose single main street keeps many of its civic and heritage buildings.

placements.name: West Coast Heritage Centre
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=museum 'West Coast Heritage Centre'
placements.reason: Small Zeehan museum; one source only and low views (324), kept by the merged skeptic.
placements.bio: A small museum on Zeehan's Main Street about life on Tasmania's West Coast in the early 20th century.

placements.name: Hogarth Falls
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon waterway=waterfall 'Hogarth Falls'; People's Park folded in
placements.reason: A short walk from Strahan's People's Park.
placements.bio: A small cascade reached by a 30-minute rainforest walk from People's Park at the north end of Strahan Harbour.

placements.name: Nelson Falls
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin LOW (single photon waterway=waterfall 'Nelson Falls', 1.4 km from the footway; waterfall is a precise feature type: treat as MEDIUM pending confirmation)
placements.reason: Named by Wikivoyage as the main draw of Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park; a short boardwalk walk off the Lyell Highway, so it belongs to the park, not to West Coast.
placements.bio: A roughly 30 m waterfall on the Nelson River, reached by a short boardwalk walk off the Lyell Highway.

placements.name: Frenchmans Cap Track
placements.coordinates_source: photon amenity=parking 'Frenchmans Cap Carpark': TRAILHEAD only. Trail rule needs the route midpoint, to be taken from the agency route map in Pipeline C
placements.reason: Multi-day walk from the Lyell Highway to Frenchmans Cap, inside the park.
placements.bio: A hard 3-5 day walk from the Lyell Highway to the white quartzite summit of Frenchmans Cap.

placements.name: Donaghys Hill Lookout
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin LOW: photon tourism=viewpoint 'Donaghys Lookout' (single precise feature of the right type)
placements.reason: A 30-40 minute return walk off the Lyell Highway into the park.
placements.bio: A 30-40 minute return walk to a wilderness lookout over the Franklin River Valley.

placements.name: Franklin River
placements.coordinates_source: none: no feature found by resolve-pin; Wikipedia -42.59,145.74 is a river point far south of the road. Pin at the Lyell Highway crossing from Parks Tasmania, to be found in Pipeline C
placements.reason: Visited mainly on guided 8-9 day rafting expeditions; place it at the Lyell Highway crossing where non-rafters reach it.
placements.bio: A wild river in the World Heritage area, famed for guided multi-day rafting expeditions through its gorges.

placements.name: Gordon Dam
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin LOW: photon tourism=viewpoint 'Gordon Dam Lookout' (single precise feature, pin on the lookout)
placements.reason: At Strathgordon at the end of the Gordon River Road, inside Southwest NP's span (about 19 km from the park centre).
placements.bio: A 140 m-high arch dam at Strathgordon with a lookout over Lake Gordon and the Gordon River gorge.

placements.name: Lake Pedder
placements.coordinates_source: photon water=reservoir 'Lake Pedder' (waterbody centroid, not a visitor point). Visitor lookout/Scotts Peak Dam point to be confirmed in Pipeline C
placements.reason: Reached by the Gordon River Road and Scotts Peak Road within Southwest NP.
placements.bio: A large lake in the Southwest National Park with a lodge on its shore, viewed from lookouts and by boat.

placements.name: South Coast Track
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin LOW: photon highway=path 'South Coast Track' (one segment of the route; not a computed midpoint). Take the route midpoint from Parks Tasmania in Pipeline C
placements.reason: An 85 km walk between Melaleuca and Cockle Creek inside Southwest NP; owner of this track is this region.
placements.bio: An 85 km coastal walk through the park's wild south coast, usually six to eight days one way.

placements.name: Lake St Clair
placements.coordinates_source: photon information office 'Lake St Clair Visitor Centre' (Cynthia Bay); NOT the candidate point (-82.67 lng is the Michigan lake)
placements.reason: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park is owned by tas-northwest-cradle. If that region proposes a Cradle Mountain/park destination whose span reaches Cynthia Bay (about 56 km south of Cradle Valley), re-home this and its four neighbours below as its spots; otherwise standalone. About 45 km from the proposed Franklin-Gordon centre, past its span.
placements.bio: Australia's deepest freshwater lake, with a visitor centre at Cynthia Bay at the southern end of the Overland Track.

placements.name: Echo Point
placements.coordinates_source: photon 'Echo Point Hut' / 'Echo Point Track' on the Lake St Clair shore; single source, LOW: check it is the Great Short Walk lookout, not only the hut
placements.reason: Great Short Walk on the lake; see Lake St Clair re-homing note.
placements.bio: A lake-shore lookout on a 3-7 hour circuit from Cynthia Bay, with views over Lake St Clair.

placements.name: Overland Track
placements.coordinates_source: photon highway=path 'Overland Track' (one segment, roughly mid-route; midpoint to be computed from the agency route)
placements.reason: The 65 km walk's southern end lies here, its other end at Cradle Mountain (owner region tas-northwest-cradle): spot of that destination if proposed, else standalone. Duplicate risk with the NW region: reconcile on id.
placements.bio: Tasmania's best-known walk, about 65 km from Cradle Mountain to Lake St Clair, usually over six days.

placements.name: Mount Ossa
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=peak 'Mount Ossa' agrees with the OSM peak node
placements.reason: Inside Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park, about 30 km from Lake St Clair: a side trip from the Overland Track. Also in the NW region (flagged duplicate); this region keeps it per CROSS-REGION.
placements.bio: Tasmania's highest peak at 1,617 m, climbed on a side track from Pelion Gap on the Overland Track.

placements.name: The Wall in the Wilderness
placements.coordinates_source: photon tourism=attraction 'The Wall in the Wilderness', Derwent Bridge (single source)
placements.reason: At Derwent Bridge on the Lyell Highway, 7 km east of Lake St Clair; reached from the highway, not from a base. Within about 37 km of the Franklin-Gordon proposed centre but outside its span (45 km): it lies in the Central Highlands on the other side of the Cradle-Lake St Clair park, and Derwent Bridge village is dropped as a wrapper.
placements.bio: A roughly 100 m wall of carved Huon pine panels at Derwent Bridge telling the region's history.

placements.name: Arthur-Pieman Conservation Area
placements.coordinates_source: photon leisure=nature_reserve (area centroid, LOW); visitor point to be set from Parks Tasmania
placements.reason: 1,030 km2 of wild Tarkine coast, about 90 km from the West Coast destination: not a spot of it. May fold into a Tarkine destination if the NW region proposes one (Takayna/Tarkine is a review there).
placements.bio: A 1,030 km2 stretch of wild Tarkine coast of dunes, beaches and shack communities between the Arthur and Pieman rivers.

placements.name: Edge of the World
placements.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=attraction 'Edge of the World'
placements.reason: The Arthur River mouth viewpoint; kept as its own named stop beside the conservation area, standalone for the same reason (no destination within 90 km).
placements.bio: The Arthur River mouth headland on Tasmania's wild west coast, a named lookout over the open Southern Ocean.

Beyond the span and inside Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park (a different park, owned by tas-northwest-cradle).

standalone_vs_destination_checks.why_not_a_spot: Inside Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park, not Franklin-Gordon; a national park is never a spot of another park.
